points.title: 童年教育
points.description: 1500年2月24日，查理出生于根特，是哈布斯堡家族的成员。作为勃艮第公爵菲利普一世和卡斯蒂利亚女王胡安娜的儿子，他从小接受多语言教育，掌握法语、荷兰语、德语、西班牙语和拉丁语。他的童年主要在低地国家度过，由多位教师教导，包括人文主义学者。这段经历培养了他对艺术的热爱和广泛的国际视野，也让他认识到统治多民族国家的复杂性。
points.descriptionEn: Born on February 24, 1500, in Ghent, Charles was a member of the House of Habsburg. As the son of Philip I of Burgundy and Joanna of Castile, he received a multilingual education, mastering French, Dutch, German, Spanish, and Latin. His childhood was primarily spent in the Low Countries, where he was taught by several instructors, including humanist scholars. This period fostered his appreciation for the arts and his broad international perspective, while also exposing him to the complexities of ruling a multi-ethnic empire.

points.title: 继承勃艮第与西班牙
points.description: 1516年，查理继承了外祖父斐迪南二世的西班牙王位，成为卡斯蒂利亚和阿拉贡的国王，统治西班牙及其广阔的海外殖民地。同时，他也继承了勃艮第公爵领地，包括低地国家。在布鲁塞尔，他开始学习统治技巧，面对西班牙贵族的挑战和低地国家的复杂政治局势。这一时期，他任命威廉·德·克罗伊作为顾问，开始建立自己的统治团队，为日后管理庞大帝国做准备。
points.descriptionEn: In 1516, Charles inherited the Spanish throne from his maternal grandfather Ferdinand II, becoming King of Castile and Aragon, ruling Spain and its vast overseas territories. Simultaneously, he inherited the Burgundian territories, including the Low Countries. In Brussels, he began learning the art of governance, facing challenges from Spanish nobility and the complex political situation in the Low Countries. During this period, he appointed William de Croÿ as his advisor and began building his administrative team, preparing for the future management of his vast empire.

points.place: 布鲁塞尔/维也纳/托莱多
points.title: 神圣罗马皇帝
points.description: 1519年，查理当选神圣罗马帝国皇帝，成为欧洲历史上权力最大的君主之一。他的领土横跨欧洲、美洲和亚洲，包括西班牙、尼德兰、德意志、意大利南部、美洲殖民地和菲律宾等地。作为皇帝，他面临宗教改革、奥斯曼帝国威胁和法国的挑战。他多次召开帝国会议，试图改革帝国结构，但成效有限。1547年，他在米尔贝格战役中击败新教联盟，但未能彻底解决宗教分裂问题。这一时期，他频繁在布鲁塞尔、维也纳和托莱多之间移动，管理庞大的帝国。
points.descriptionEn: In 1519, Charles was elected Holy Roman Emperor, becoming one of the most powerful monarchs in European history. His territories spanned Europe, the Americas, and Asia, including Spain, the Netherlands, Germany, southern Italy, American colonies, and the Philippines. As emperor, he faced the Protestant Reformation, Ottoman threats, and challenges from France. He convened multiple imperial diets to reform the empire's structure with limited success. In 1547, he defeated Protestant forces at the Battle of Mühlberg but failed to resolve religious divisions. During this period, he frequently moved between Brussels, Vienna, and Toledo to govern his vast empire.

points.title: 对抗宗教改革
points.description: 1521年，查理五世在沃尔姆斯帝国会议上面对马丁·路德，要求他放弃异端观点，否则将被逐出教会。这一决定标志着查理与宗教改革运动的决裂。尽管查理本人是天主教虔诚的支持者，但他更关心帝国的统一和稳定。他多次试图通过宗教会议解决分裂问题，包括1541年的雷根斯堡会议。1545年，他召集特兰托会议，试图改革天主教会并回应新教诉求，但会议进展缓慢。查理对宗教改革的态度体现了他在宗教原则与政治现实之间的艰难平衡。
points.descriptionEn: In 1521, Charles V faced Martin Luther at the Diet of Worms, demanding he recant his heretical views or face excommunication. This decision marked Charles's break with the Reformation movement. Despite being a devout Catholic, Charles was more concerned with imperial unity and stability. He attempted to resolve the division through multiple religious conferences, including the Regensburg Conference of 1541. In 1545, he convened the Council of Trent, aiming to reform the Catholic Church and address Protestant concerns, though progress was slow. Charles's approach to the Reformation reflected his difficult balance between religious principles and political realities.

points.title: 对抗奥斯曼帝国
points.description: 面对奥斯曼帝国苏莱曼大帝的扩张威胁，查理五世多次组织军事行动。1535年，他亲率军队攻占突尼斯，暂时遏制了奥斯曼在北非的扩张。1541年，他试图占领阿尔及尔，但遭遇风暴失败。1547年，他与奥斯曼帝国达成和平协议，但冲突持续。在地中海地区，查理建立了海军联盟，包括热那亚、教皇国和马耳他骑士团，共同对抗奥斯曼海军。这些军事行动虽然未能彻底解决奥斯曼威胁，但保护了欧洲南部边境和地中海贸易路线，展现了查理作为基督教世界领袖的角色。
points.descriptionEn: Facing the expansion threat from Ottoman Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent, Charles V organized multiple military campaigns. In 1535, he personally led an army to capture Tunis, temporarily curbing Ottoman expansion in North Africa. In 1541, he attempted to capture Algiers but failed due to a storm. In 1547, he reached a peace agreement with the Ottomans, but conflicts continued. In the Mediterranean, Charles established a naval alliance including Genoa, the Papal States, and the Knights of Malta to counter the Ottoman navy. Although these campaigns failed to completely resolve the Ottoman threat, they protected Europe's southern borders and Mediterranean trade routes, demonstrating Charles's role as leader of the Christian world.

points.title: 退隐与逝世
points.description: 1556年，面对持续的健康问题和帝国管理的巨大压力，查理五世决定退位。他将西班牙及其殖民地传给儿子菲利普二世，神圣罗马帝国传给弟弟斐迪南一世。退隐后，他前往西班牙的尤斯特修道院，过着简朴的宗教生活。在修道院中，他专注于祈祷、阅读和园艺活动，偶尔仍关注政治发展。1558年9月21日，查理五世在尤斯特修道院逝世，享年58岁。他的退隐象征着欧洲权力格局的重大转变，也反映了这位曾经统治半个世界的君主在晚年寻求内心平静的愿望。
points.descriptionEn: In 1556, facing ongoing health issues and the immense pressure of imperial governance, Charles V decided to abdicate. He transmitted Spain and its colonies to his son Philip II, and the Holy Roman Empire to his brother Ferdinand I. After abdication, he retired to the Yuste Monastery in Spain, living a simple religious life. There, he focused on prayer, reading, and gardening, occasionally keeping informed about political developments. Charles V died at Yuste Monastery on September 21, 1558, at the age of 58. His retirement symbolized a major shift in European power dynamics and reflected the former ruler of half the world's desire for inner peace in his final years.

appraisal.zh: 查理五世通常被视为欧洲历史上最强大的君主之一，他维护天主教统一、抵御奥斯曼扩张，建立起横跨欧亚美的庞大帝国，其统治推动文化交流与经济繁荣，为西班牙黄金时代奠基，也标志着欧洲权力由地中海向大西洋转移。但另一种看法认为，他的统治过于专制集权，以武力压制宗教改革导致欧洲长期分裂与宗教战争，财政过度依赖美洲殖民地财富，频繁军事行动耗尽国库，殖民政策剥削原住民；帝国缺乏有效中央管理，退位后迅速解体，暴露出统治模式的根本缺陷。
appraisal.en: Charles V is generally seen as one of the most powerful monarchs in European history: he defended Catholic unity, checked Ottoman expansion, and built an empire spanning Europe, Asia and the Americas, fostering cultural exchange and prosperity, laying the groundwork for Spain's Golden Age, and marking the shift of European power from the Mediterranean to the Atlantic. Yet another view holds that his rule was excessively autocratic, that suppressing the Reformation by force bred lasting division and religious war, that finances depended too heavily on American colonial wealth and frequent campaigns exhausted the treasury, and that colonial exploitation and the lack of effective central administration left an empire that fragmented soon after his abdication.

supporter.zh: 查理五世被视为欧洲历史上最伟大的君主之一，他成功维护了天主教信仰的统一，对抗奥斯曼帝国的扩张，并建立了横跨欧亚美的庞大帝国。他的统治促进了欧洲各地区的文化交流和经济繁荣，为西班牙的黄金时代奠定了基础。查理五世还推动了艺术和科学的发展，支持探险家开拓新航线，扩大了欧洲的世界影响力。他作为神圣罗马帝国皇帝，努力维护帝国的传统和权威，体现了中世纪欧洲君主制的理想。
supporter.en: Charles V is regarded as one of the greatest monarchs in European history, successfully preserving Catholic unity, countering Ottoman expansion, and establishing a vast empire spanning Europe, Asia, and the Americas. His rule promoted cultural exchange and economic prosperity across European regions, laying the foundation for Spain's Golden Age. Charles V also advanced arts and sciences, supported explorers in opening new trade routes, and expanded Europe's global influence. As Holy Roman Emperor, he worked to maintain imperial traditions and authority, embodying the ideal of medieval European monarchy.

critic.zh: 批评者认为查理五世的统治过于专制和集权，他试图通过武力手段压制宗教改革，导致欧洲长期分裂和宗教战争。他的财政政策过度依赖美洲殖民地的财富，最终导致西班牙经济衰退。查理五世频繁的军事行动耗尽了国库，使帝国陷入财政危机。此外，他对美洲原住民的剥削和殖民政策也受到严厉批评。他的帝国虽然广阔，但缺乏有效的中央管理，最终在他退位后迅速解体，证明了他的统治模式存在根本缺陷。
critic.en: Critics argue that Charles V's rule was excessively autocratic and centralized. His attempts to suppress the Reformation by force led to prolonged European religious divisions and wars. His financial policies过度依赖 on wealth from American colonies, eventually causing economic decline in Spain. His frequent military campaigns exhausted the treasury, plunging the empire into financial crisis. Additionally, his exploitation of indigenous peoples and colonial policies face severe criticism. Although his empire was vast, it lacked effective central administration and rapidly fragmented after his abdication, revealing fundamental flaws in his governing model.

objective.zh: 在历史学界，查理五世被视为一个复杂的历史人物，既是中世纪欧洲君主制的最后代表，也是现代早期国际关系的开创者。他的统治标志着欧洲权力从地中海向大西洋的转移，为后来的民族国家形成奠定了基础。在流行文化中，查理五世常被描绘为一位疲惫而孤独的君主形象，反映了权力与责任之间的永恒矛盾。他的生平被多次改编成文学作品和影视作品，如《皇帝的密使》等，展现了这位统治半个世界的君主在权力巅峰与个人救赎之间的挣扎。
objective.en: In historical scholarship, Charles V is viewed as a complex figure, representing both the culmination of medieval European monarchy and a pioneer of early modern international relations. His rule marked the transfer of European power from the Mediterranean to the Atlantic, laying foundations for later nation-state formation. In popular culture, Charles is often depicted as a weary and lonely monarch, reflecting the eternal tension between power and responsibility. His life has been adapted into numerous literary works and films, such as 'The Emperor's Ambassador,' portraying the struggles of this ruler of half the world between his peak of power and personal redemption.

self.zh: 我宁愿统治一个贫穷但和平的国家，也不愿统治一个富裕但不断战乱的国家。
self.en: I would rather rule a poor and peaceful country than a rich and constantly warring one.
